articles.title: Volunteers Turn Out for the Summer Cleanup Across Lower Millrace
articles.deck: Residents of Lower Millrace filled the hall on Saturday to ask questions about the plan.
body: The Lower Millrace Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
Public works estimates the work will take about 32 weeks once it begins.

Dana Jurgens, who has lived in Lower Millrace for 32 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Saturday mornings.

articles.title: St. Brendan’s Parish Announces New Hours for Summer

body: The group has raised $48,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. The Hickory Ridge Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
Esther Quinlan, who has lived in Hickory Ridge for 28 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. Public works estimates the work will take about 28 weeks once it begins.

articles.title: Dolores Kim, 82, Volunteer Firefighter
articles.deck: Friends remember Dolores Kim for the many years of service to Kettle Hill.
body: Born in Kettle Hill in the years after the war, Dolores Kim spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood. Dolores Kim died in February at home on Orchard Lane, at the age of 82.

Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Foxglove Heights Neighbors in his or her name. Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Kettle Hill.

articles.title: Library Adds Sidewalk Ramp This Summer
articles.deck: Doors open at 6 p.m. and the event is free to the public.
body: Doors open at 6 p.m. and the event is free to the public. Organizers ask guests to bring a dish to share or a little cash for supplies.
Children are welcome, and volunteers will be on hand to help with parking and set-up.

articles.title: Letters: Briar Drive Parking Is Out of Control
body: To the editor: I have lived on Briar Drive for 17 years, and I want to say what a difference the Canal Park Food Pantry has made. I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the February meeting.
Please keep the community garden in the budget. Many of us on Briar Drive use it every week.
Nadia Hobart, Hickory Ridge

articles.title: Then & Now: Briar Avenue in 1991 and Today
articles.deck: A photo from the Millrace County Historical Society shows the same corner as it looked decades ago.
body: Most of the houses are still standing, though the porches and the trees have changed a good deal. Someone took the same picture from the same spot this month, holding the camera at about the same height.
A 1991 photograph from the Millrace County Historical Society shows Briar Avenue from the corner of Pearl Avenue.

articles.title: Tannery Flats Asks Council for Speed Limit Change
articles.deck: The vote came after 39 residents spoke at Sunday’s session.
body: Councilmember Sergio Novak asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $3,400. Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.
